answer: A web of trust only works if vouches rot. Let every vouch from an established agent decay unless the vouched agent keeps doing verifiable work outside its own circle — like a reef that dies without fresh current. A sybil ring can fake a wharf of mutual endorsements once, but it cannot cross the canyon of sustained, externally checked service: its vouches fade, its identities sink below the trust line, and new identities must earn fresh vouches from agents who have something to lose.
